questions.text: What percentage of classes must WKU students attend?
questions.hint: "Students must attend at least 80% of all classes."

questions.text: Students at WKU are required to wear a uniform.
questions.hint: "Students don't have to wear a uniform."

questions.text: What happens to students who commit plagiarism or cheat?
questions.hint: "Students who cheat may be expelled from the university."

questions.text: Dormitory residents must sign in if they return after ___ pm.
questions.hint: "You have to sign in and out of the dormitory if you return after 11pm."

questions.text: Is joining a club at WKU mandatory?
opts: No, it is optional but recommended
questions.correct: No, it is optional but recommended
questions.hint: "You don't have to join a club or society, but it is strongly recommended."

questions.text: "Plagiarism" means:
opts: Copying work and presenting it as your own
questions.correct: Copying work and presenting it as your own
questions.hint: Plagiarism = presenting someone else's work as your own without acknowledgement.

questions.text: What mistake did Zhibek make?
opts: She submitted an old draft instead of the final version
questions.correct: She submitted an old draft instead of the final version
questions.hint: Zhibek accidentally submitted an old draft instead of the final essay version.

questions.text: What does Amir say Zhibek should do first?
opts: Post about it on social media
questions.hint: "You should email your lecturer immediately."

questions.text: What order does Amir recommend for preparing a presentation?
questions.hint: "You should plan your structure first, then research, then practise."

questions.text: Amir says tired people make fewer mistakes.
questions.hint: Amir said "Tired people make MORE mistakes."

questions.text: What type of planner does Amir recommend?
questions.hint: "a planner — digital or paper, whatever works for you."

questions.text: You ___ email the lecturer immediately.
questions.hint: "should" + BASE form. No changes for any subject.

questions.text: You ___ panic — it's a small mistake.
questions.hint: Negative advice: shouldn't + BASE form.

questions.text: Students ___ use phones during lectures.
questions.hint: "mustn't" = prohibited / not allowed.

questions.text: Students ___ wear a uniform — there isn't one.
questions.hint: "don't have to" = no obligation / optional.

questions.text: "mustn't" and "don't have to" mean the same thing.
questions.hint: "mustn't" = forbidden. "don't have to" = optional. They are OPPOSITES.

questions.text: She ___ retake the exam last year. (past obligation)
questions.hint: "must" has no past form → use "had to" for past obligation.

questions.text: "must" vs "have to" — which expresses the speaker's own authority?
questions.hint: "must" = speaker's own feeling/authority. "have to" = external rule.

questions.text: "prohibited" means:
questions.hint: "Prohibited" = officially not allowed.

questions.text: "plagiarism" means studying very hard.
questions.hint: "Plagiarism" = copying someone else's work and claiming it as your own.

questions.text: "draft" refers to:
opts: The final version of a document
A first or early version of a document
questions.correct: A first or early version of a document
questions.hint: "Draft" = an early, unfinished version of a piece of writing.

questions.text: "extracurricular" activities are:
opts: Activities outside the normal academic curriculum
questions.correct: Activities outside the normal academic curriculum
questions.hint: "Extracurricular" = activities beyond the formal academic programme (clubs, sports, etc.).

questions.text: "designated area" means:
opts: An officially set aside area for a specific purpose
questions.correct: An officially set aside area for a specific purpose
questions.hint: "Designated" = officially chosen or set aside for a particular purpose.

questions.text: She accidentally submitted an old ___ instead of the final version.
questions.hint: "Draft" = a first or early version of a document, not the final one.

questions.text: "violation" means:
opts: The act of breaking a rule or law
questions.correct: The act of breaking a rule or law
questions.hint: "Violation" = the act of breaking a rule, law, or agreement.

questions.text: "structure" in the context of an essay means:
questions.hint: "Structure" = the way something is organised or arranged.

questions.text: "expelled" means you won a scholarship.
questions.hint: "Expelled" = required to leave a school or university due to breaking the rules.

questions.text: A "planner" is used to:
questions.hint: "Planner" = a book or app used to organise your daily tasks and schedule.

questions.text: "submission" means:
opts: Presenting a piece of work to someone
questions.correct: Presenting a piece of work to someone
questions.hint: "Submission" = the act of presenting or handing in a piece of work.

questions.text: It's a small mistake, not an academic ___.
questions.hint: "Violation" = breaking a rule. A small mistake ≠ an academic violation.
